Galitsky, C., Chang, S., Worrell, E. and Masanet, E. (2008). Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for the Pharmaceutical Industry: An ENERGY STAR Guide for Energy and Plant Managers. Report LBNL-57260-Revision, Ernest Orlando Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA, March 2008. No DOI or URL printed.

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 8). An ENERGY STAR measure catalogue for U.S. pharmaceutical plants (HVAC, fume hoods, cleanrooms, motors, compressed air, pumps, refrigeration, lighting, steam, CHP); almost every number is reprinted from other sources and there are no energy intensities per unit of product. Main file (11 technologies, 12 examples in 7 contexts): steam-turbine and gas-turbine CHP overall efficiency (HHV), gas-turbine electrical efficiency, heat-to-power derived from printed power-to-heat ratios, STIG minimum size, absorption chiller capacity range (tons converted to kW) and absorption/adsorption COP, micro back-pressure let-down turbine (output pressure; 13.5 kWh/MBtu steam in _flows), a boiler house with feed-water and air preheat approaching 95% (Merck Elkton case), exhaust-air heat recovery effectiveness for heat wheels, heat pipes and run-around loops, and a gas engine-driven air compressor case (capex per hp derived from unit costs). _measures.csv: all quantified measures of Chapter 5 with saving, cost and payback as printed (nominal USD, price years not printed). _other-values.csv: Table 3 energy-use shares by end use and activity, sector statistics, cleanroom and compressed-air shares, rules of thumb, and the J&J La Jolla trigeneration plant (prime mover not stated). Not loaded: Figures 5-7 (charts, values not printed), company and state tables (Tables 1-2), qualitative measures, Appendices A-C.

(1) No price year for any cost; case-study costs come from sources dated 1995-2005. (2) Heating-value basis given only for CHP overall efficiencies (HHV); the gas-turbine electrical efficiency 27-37% has no basis. (3) The "efficiency" of heat wheels, heat pipes and run-around loops is heat-exchange effectiveness. (4) Two figures are numbered "Figure 7" (electricity consumption, p.15; energy management elements, p.20). (5) Section 5.2 refers to heat and steam distribution as Section 5.9 (it is 5.10). (6) Vortex hood saving is a manufacturer claim. (7) The trigeneration absorption cycle is described with hydrogen gas (a diffusion-absorption cycle), not the usual industrial water-ammonia or LiBr chiller.
